doc.title: Pete Candoli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999

title: Touring Japan with Benny Carter
summary: Pete describes the warm welcome and knowledgeable fans in Japan and Europe.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: What has your experience been overseas?

Fine. The reception of course, they know more about an artist over there then they do here in the States. It’s like one time I went over with Benny Carter, with different players, you know Frank Wess and really some wonderful players. And had about maybe ten, twelve concerts, and we landed at Narita airport, and there’s white sheets from a bed, king size probably, all strung together “Welcome Pete Candoli and Blackwell and Benny Carter, all the guy’s names and we got all the people applauding, fans, they know who played third trumpet on one tune and who played lead, who took the solo?

In Japan. And they know this, they make a study of this, to them it’s history, and they know every artist, where it was recorded, the year, afternoon date or evening date, and right away they take you in stretch limos, Cadillacs, about six or seven of them take us to one of the major hotels, for all the press, while we’re being checked in by the management and we’re they with hors d’oeuvres and talking and they’re shooting pictures, just like you’d think the Rolling Stones came to town. And even in Europe, that’s how they acknowledge the players. They know who you are.
